title_en: He Ronglan v. Haike Company et al. — dispute over debt repayment
keywords_en: civil; dispute over contract for assignment of creditor's rights; second instance; Supreme People's Court; Shandong Province; natural person; legal person; Contract Law; method of notice for assignment of creditor's rights; validity of notice by newspaper publication; performance of debt; affirm the original judgment; assignment of creditor's rights; notice by newspaper publication; debt guarantee; good faith; dispute over debt repayment against Haike Company and others
full_text_en:
He Ronglan v. Haike Company et al. — Dispute over Debt Liquidation

[【Ruling Summary】]

The provision of Article 80, Paragraph 1 of the Contract Law is intended to prevent the debtor from performing the debt repeatedly, erroneously, or with increased burden. It does not violate the law for a creditor to notify the debtor via newspaper publication. As long as the creditor has effectively made the notification, the assignment of the claim shall be legally binding on the debtor.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2003) Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 46

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Dongying Haike Chemical Industry Co., Ltd., domiciled at the west side of Haochun Road, Dongying District, Dongying City, Shandong Province.

Legal Representative: Yang Xiaohong, Chairperson of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Cai Zhongjie, Attorney at Shandong Kangqiao Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Jin Rongkui, Attorney at Shandong Kangqiao Law Firm.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): He Ronglan, female, born on September 2, 1967, Han ethnicity, residing at Building 6, Northern Area, Yanzishan Subdistrict, Lixia District, Jinan City, Shandong Province.

Agent ad litem: Yu Jie, female, born on May 14, 1972, Han ethnicity, residing at No. 36 Yuhan Road, Jinan City, Shandong Province.

Agent ad litem: Yu Fushun, male, born on September 23, 1963, Han ethnicity, residing at No. 52 Yanzishan East Road, Jinan City, Shandong Province.

Defendant at First Instance: Dongying Cement Products Factory, domiciled at the west end of Huanghe Road, Dongying City, Shandong Province.

Legal Representative: Tian Zhenrong, Factory Manager.

Agent ad litem: Liu Jun, Attorney at Shandong Huanghe Law Firm, Dongying Branch.

Defendant at First Instance: Dongying Huanghekou Building Materials Development Corporation, domiciled at the west end of Huanghe Road, Dongying City, Shandong Province.

Legal Representative: Tian Zhenrong, Manager of the Corporation.

In the case of dispute over debt liquidation between appellant Dongying Haike Chemical Industry Co., Ltd. and appellee He Ronglan, defendants at first instance Dongying Cement Products Factory and Dongying Huanghekou Building Materials Development Corporation, the Shandong High People's Court rendered a civil judgment (2003) Lu Min Yi Chu Zi No. 4 on June 2, 2003. The appellant Dongying Haike Chemical Industry Co., Ltd. was dissatisfied and appealed to this Court. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel and held a public hearing on August 7, 2003. The agent ad litem of appellant Dongying Haike Chemical Industry Co., Ltd., Cai Zhongjie and Jin Rongkui; the agent ad litem of appellee He Ronglan, Yu Jie and Yu Fushun; and the agent ad litem of defendant at first instance Dongying Cement Products Factory, Liu Jun, appeared in court. This case has now been concluded.

The court of first instance found the following facts after trial:

On August 24, December 2, and December 5, 1994, Dongying Cement Products Factory (hereinafter referred to as Cement Products Factory) borrowed RMB 1 million, RMB 930,000, and RMB 70,000 respectively from the Hekou District Sub-branch of the Agricultural Bank of China, Dongying City, for the purchase of cement and steel, with agreed interest rates of 10.98‰ and 14.64‰ respectively. If the loan was not repaid at maturity, an additional 20% interest would be charged on the overdue loan. The above loans were all guaranteed by Dongying Huanghekou Building Materials Development Corporation (hereinafter referred to as Building Materials Corporation).

On December 24, 1996, Cement Products Factory borrowed RMB 10.5 million from the Dongying District Sub-branch of the Agricultural Bank of China, Dongying City, for the purchase of cement product materials, with a term of one year from December 24, 1996 to December 24, 1997, at an interest rate of 9.24‰ per month. Article 2 of the contract stipulated that Cement Products Factory should repay the principal and interest of the loan within the agreed term. Overdue loan would accrue interest at a daily rate of 0.4‰ during the overdue period. If an extension was needed, Cement Products Factory must submit an extension application ten days before the loan maturity date. Upon approval, an extension agreement would be signed. Once the extension agreement was signed, its effect would extend to the guarantor, who voluntarily continued to assume the guarantee obligation, and the original guarantee period would be correspondingly extended. Article 5 of the contract stipulated that the guarantor and the borrower jointly assumed joint and several liability. The guarantee period of the guarantor was: from the effective date of this contract to two years after the maturity date of the last loan, i.e., from December 24, 1997 to December 24, 1999. The guarantee was provided by Dongying Haike Chemical Industry Co., Ltd. (formerly Shandong Dongying Petrochemical Plant, hereinafter referred to as Haike Company).

On December 24, 1997, the Dongying District Sub-branch of the Agricultural Bank of China, Dongying City, together with Cement Products Factory and Haike Company, signed the (97) Nong Yin Bao Jie Yan Xie Zi No. 00013 "Guaranteed Loan Extension Agreement," stipulating that Cement Products Factory had borrowed RMB 10.5 million from the lender on December 24, 1996, which was due for repayment of all principal and interest on December 24, 1997. Due to capital shortage, it could not be repaid on time, and upon negotiation among the parties, it was agreed to extend the repayment to March 24, 1998. The "Loan Contract" signed on December 24, 1996 was an inseparable part of this agreement. All terms of the original Loan Contract remained valid for this agreement. In case of conflict between this agreement and the terms of the original Loan Contract, this agreement shall prevail. Haike Company, as guarantor, affixed its seal to the agreement in acknowledgment.

On June 20, 1998, the Hekou District Sub-branch of the Agricultural Bank of China, Dongying City, issued a notice of overdue loan recovery to Cement Products Factory, stating that a loan of RMB 2 million had matured. As of June 20, 1998, the unit still owed the bank loan principal and interest totaling RMB 2.25 million, constituting a breach of contract, and requested immediate repayment of all loan principal and interest. Cement Products Factory and the guarantor Building Materials Corporation affixed their seals to the notice on June 22, 1998. On November 29, 1999, the Shandong Provincial Sub-branch of the Agricultural Bank of China issued Notice No. 25 for recovery of overdue loans, stating: The loan of RMB 10.5 million from December 24, 1996, matured on March 24, 1998. Please prepare funds and go to the bank to handle repayment procedures on time, otherwise it will be dealt with according to the contract. On December 22, 1999, Cement Products Factory issued a receipt for Notice No. 25, stating: Received on December 22, 1999. Comments: Raise funds as soon as possible to repay the bank loan. Cement Products Factory affixed its official seal. The legal representative of the guarantor also signed and affixed the official seal, with the date of March 23, 2000.

On December 20, 1999, the Hekou District Sub-branch of the Agricultural Bank of China, Dongying City, issued a notice of overdue loan recovery to Cement Products Factory, stating: "The loan of RMB 2 million has matured. As of December 20, 1999, your unit still owes our bank loan principal and interest totaling RMB 2.33 million. Please immediately repay all loan principal and interest to our bank." Cement Products Factory and the guarantor Building Materials Corporation affixed their seals to the notice on December 22, 1999.

On March 10, 2000, the Shandong Provincial Sub-branch of the Agricultural Bank of China and the Jinan Office of China Great Wall Asset Management Corporation signed the "Agreement on Stripping and Acquiring Non-Performing Assets," stipulating that the debts owed by debtor Cement Products Factory and guarantor Building Materials Corporation to the Agricultural Bank of China amounted to RMB 2,398,520 in principal and interest as specified, and the debts owed by debtor Cement Products Factory and guarantor Haike Company to the Agricultural Bank of China amounted to RMB 12,270,874.12 in principal and interest as specified, with the claims transferring to China Great Wall Asset Management Corporation from March 25, 2000. The transfer was notified to the debtor and guarantors by (Ji) Zhong Chang Zi Zhai Zi (2000) No. 050300002 and (Ji) Zhong Chang Zi Zhai Zi (2000) No. 050200027 confirmations, respectively, requiring the debtor and guarantors to voluntarily repay all the above debts to China Great Wall Asset Management Corporation or formulate a repayment plan upon receipt of the confirmation. Cement Products Factory and Building Materials Corporation, in the receipt of confirmation (Ji) Zhong Chang Zi Zhai Zi (2000) No. 050300002, and Cement Products Factory and Haike Company, in the receipt of confirmation (Ji) Zhong Chang Zi Zhai Zi (2000) No. 050200027, expressly stated that they had no objection to the assignment of the claims and that the borrower and guarantor guaranteed to continue performing all obligations under the loan contracts, guarantee contracts, or agreements. Building Materials Corporation signed on June 3, 2000; Haike Company signed on March 23, 2000.

On May 31, 2000, Haike Company issued a certificate to the Dongying District Sub-branch of the Agricultural Bank of China, Dongying City, stating: "Our unit has provided guarantees for Cement Products Factory's loans from your bank on multiple occasions, and provided guarantee for the rollover loan of RMB 10.5 million for this enterprise on December 24, 1996. This is hereby stated." On March 12, 2002, a debt collection announcement was published on page 14 of Shandong Legal News, requiring Cement Products Factory, Building Materials Corporation, and Haike Company to perform their repayment obligations.

On September 30, 2002, the Jinan Office of China Great Wall Asset Management Corporation, pursuant to the reply on the approval of the transfer of claims against Cement Products Factory, Zhong Chang Zi Fu (2002) No. 386, signed the claim transfer agreement (2002) Zhong Chang Zi Ji Zhai Zhuan Zi No. 003 with He Ronglan, stipulating that five loan claims (and ancillary rights) owed by Cement Products Factory were transferred to He Ronglan, with a list of transferred claims attached. On January 21, 2003, the Jinan Office of China Great Wall Asset Management Corporation and He Ronglan published a notice of claim transfer on page 2 of Shandong Legal News, informing Cement Products Factory and the guarantors Building Materials Corporation and Haike Company that the claim principal of RMB 12.6 million and corresponding interest owed by Cement Products Factory, as well as all ancillary rights thereunder, had been legally transferred to He Ronglan, who would exercise all rights of the creditor. Upon receipt of this notice, they should actively perform repayment obligations to He Ronglan.

Second, the issue of whether the guarantee liability period for Haike Company has expired. Haike Company claimed that, according to the contract, its guarantee liability period was from December 24, 1997 to December 24, 1999. Haike Company signed the receipt for the confirmation notice of assignment of creditor's rights on March 3, 2000. Pursuant to Articles 31 and 44 of the Judicial Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Guarantee Law and the Reply of the Supreme People's Court Letter (2002) No. 3, Haike Company should not bear guarantee liability. Even if the assignment agreement of creditor's rights between He Ronglan and the Jinan Office of China Great Wall Asset Management Corporation became legally effective as to Haike Company, Haike Company should not bear guarantee liability after the expiration of the guarantee period. The court of first instance held: First, Article 31 of the Judicial Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Guarantee Law provides that the guarantee period shall not be interrupted, suspended, or extended for any reason. The guarantee period and the statute of limitations are two different concepts and cannot be confused. Article 44 of the said Judicial Interpretation does not apply to this case, as this case is not a bankruptcy case. The Reply of the Supreme People's Court Letter (2002) No. 3 mainly clarifies the issue of interruption of the statute of limitations and does not affect the valid exercise of He Ronglan's litigation rights. Second, according to the Agreement No. (97) Nong Yin Bao Jie Yan Xie Zi No. 00013, the repayment period for the RMB 10.5 million loan was extended to March 24, 1998. Haike Company affixed its seal to this agreement, indicating its acceptance. With the extension of the loan, in accordance with the provisions of the loan contract and the guarantee contract, Haike Company's guarantee period was correspondingly extended from March 25, 1998 to March 24, 2000. Even within the original guarantee period, i.e., on November 29, 1999, the Shandong Branch of Agricultural Bank of China issued a Notice of Demand for Repayment of Overdue Loan (No. 25) to the Cement Products Factory. The Cement Products Factory and Haike Company signed and sealed the receipt for the notice of demand for repayment of overdue loan on December 22, 1999 and March 23, 2000, respectively. This Notice of Demand for Repayment of Overdue Loan proves that the creditor at that time asserted its rights against the borrower and the guarantor within the period for the guarantor to perform the guarantee liability. According to law, the statute of limitations then began to run for two years, i.e., from November 29, 1999 to November 28, 2001. Although both the guarantee period and the statute of limitations result in certain legal consequences if the creditor fails to exercise its rights within a certain period, there is a fundamental difference between them. During the guarantee period, if the creditor exercises its rights, the original legal relationship is changed, and the effect of the guarantee period is extinguished; whereas during the statute of limitations period, if the right holder exercises the right of claim, the original legal relationship is maintained and continues. Therefore, in this case, Haike Company and the Building Materials Company, as guarantors, are not exempted from guarantee liability, and the guarantee liability is no longer subject to the guarantee period but is subject to the statute of limitations. Third, from the perspective of the receipt for the confirmation notice of assignment of creditor's rights issued by the Jinan Office of China Great Wall Asset Management Corporation to the Dongying District Sub-branch of Agricultural Bank of China, the borrower and the guarantor agreed to continue to perform the obligations stipulated in the loan contract, guarantee contract, and agreements. The guarantor's seal was affixed on March 23, 2000. This notice and receipt indicate that Haike Company was still voluntarily extending the guarantee period, i.e., before March 24, 2000, the right holder again asserted its rights, clearly demanding repayment from the debtor and the guarantor. Pursuant to Article 34, paragraph 2 of the Judicial Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Guarantee Law, the statute of limitations for the Jinan Office of China Great Wall Asset Management Corporation to demand that the guarantor perform the guarantee liability began anew from March 24, 2000, i.e., from March 24, 2000 to March 23, 2002. On March 12, 2002, the Jinan Office of China Great Wall Asset Management Corporation published a public announcement in Shandong Legal News to demand repayment of creditor's rights from the creditor and the guarantor, thereby exercising its rights. At that point, the statute of limitations was interrupted according to law, and the statute of limitations began anew, i.e., from March 12, 2002 to March 11, 2004. On January 21, 2003, the Jinan Office of China Great Wall Asset Management Corporation published a notice of assignment of creditor's rights on the second page of Shandong Legal News, demanding that the new creditor He Ronglan be repaid. On February 13, 2003, the creditor He Ronglan filed a lawsuit with this court, demanding repayment of principal and interest. He Ronglan's lawsuit was filed within the statutory statute of limitations period. Therefore, Haike Company's argument that He Ronglan's lawsuit had exceeded the guarantee period and that Haike Company should not bear any legal liability cannot stand.

Third, the issue of jurisdiction over this case. The Supreme People's Court stipulates that the subject matter of first-instance civil cases accepted by the Shandong High People's Court must be at least RMB 30 million. The court of first instance accepted the case in accordance with this regulation, which does not violate the provisions of the Supreme People's Court. Moreover, pursuant to Article 39, paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, a higher people's court has the authority to hear first-instance civil cases under the jurisdiction of a lower people's court, and may also transfer first-instance civil cases under its own jurisdiction to a lower people's court for hearing. The acceptance of this case by the court of first instance is also legally grounded. Therefore, Haike Company's argument that this case should be heard by the Dongying Intermediate People's Court of Shandong Province cannot stand.

Fourth, the issue of whether this case can be consolidated for trial. In this case, the creditor is He Ronglan, and the debtor is the Cement Products Factory, with a clear creditor-debtor relationship. Although the guarantors are not the same entity, each guarantor bears its own guarantee liability in this case, and its liability is also clear. Therefore, consolidation for trial is not impermissible. Accordingly, Haike Company's argument in this regard also cannot stand.

Fifth, the issue of calculation of interest. Haike Company's claim regarding the calculation of interest should be supported according to law. The calculation of interest should be adjusted according to law. The result should be: For the RMB 10.5 million, the principal and interest before March 25, 2000 were RMB 12,270,874.12, plus interest of RMB 2,438,730 from March 21, 2000 to March 31, 2003, totaling RMB 14,709,604.12; for the RMB 2 million, the principal and interest before March 25, 2000 were RMB 2,398,520, plus interest of RMB 464,520 from March 21, 2000 to March 31, 2003, totaling RMB 2,863,040.

In summary, the judgment was as follows: (1) The Cement Products Factory shall, within ten days after the judgment takes effect, repay He Ronglan the loan principal of RMB 10.5 million and interest totaling RMB 14,709,604.12, and Haike Company shall bear joint and several liability for payment; (2) The Cement Products Factory shall, within ten days after the judgment takes effect, repay He Ronglan the loan principal of RMB 2 million and interest totaling RMB 2,863,040, and the Building Materials Company shall bear joint and several liability for payment; (3) He Ronglan's other claims were dismissed. Court costs for the first instance were RMB 168,928, to be borne by He Ronglan in the amount of RMB 76,017.60, and by the Cement Products Factory in the amount of RMB 92,910.40, of which RMB 75,257.40 shall be borne jointly and severally by Haike Company, and RMB 17,653 shall be borne jointly and severally by the Building Materials Company. Preservation fees of RMB 80,000 were to be borne by Haike Company. Appraisal fees of RMB 30,000 were to be borne by He Ronglan in the amount of RMB 10,500, and by the Cement Products Factory in the amount of RMB 19,500, of which RMB 15,015 shall be borne jointly and severally by Haike Company, and RMB 4,485 shall be borne jointly and severally by the Building Materials Company.

Haike Company, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to this court, stating: (1) The first-instance judgment had unclear findings of fact. 1. One of the defendants listed in the first-instance judgment, the Building Materials Company, no longer existed and lacked the capacity to be a party to the lawsuit. According to the business registration materials investigated by Haike Company, the Building Materials Company was renamed from the Cement Products Factory in 1993, and in December 1996, it was renamed again to the Cement Products Factory, which name has been used to date. During the first-instance proceedings, there was no corporate enterprise named the Building Materials Company in existence at all. The court of first instance erred in finding facts by listing a non-existent enterprise as a defendant in this case. 2. The first-instance finding that the loan contracts and guarantee contracts signed between the Hekou District Sub-branch of Agricultural Bank of China and the Cement Products Factory and the Building Materials Company on August 24, December 2, and December 5, 1994 were legally valid was erroneous. According to the enterprise registration records of the Dongying Branch of the Shandong Dongying Administration for Industry and Commerce, the Cement Products Factory commenced operations in June 1990, changed its name to the Building Materials Company after approval in January 1993, and changed its name back to the Cement Products Factory after approval in December 1996, which name has been used to date. Accordingly, in 1994, the Cement Products Factory had already changed its name to the Building Materials Company, and at that time, there was no enterprise named the Cement Products Factory in existence. Therefore, the loan contracts with the Cement Products Factory as the borrower and the Building Materials Company as the guarantor were invalid because the borrower no longer existed, and the guarantee contracts were also invalid. The first-instance finding that the contracts were valid was erroneous. (2) The first-instance judgment erroneously applied the law. The first-instance judgment held that the creditor's notification to the debtor of the assignment of creditor's rights by means of a newspaper announcement was in accordance with the law, which was incorrect. In this case, the original creditor, the Jinan Office of China Great Wall Asset Management Corporation, did not directly notify the debtor of the assignment of creditor's rights. As the debtor, having not received the notice of assignment, it had no legal obligation to perform the debt to the assignee. By the time the assignee He Ronglan filed the lawsuit, the assignment agreement between the Jinan Office of China Great Wall Asset Management Corporation and He Ronglan had not been notified to the debtor and thus had not taken effect as to the debtor. He Ronglan's lawsuit demanding repayment from the debtor lacked factual and legal basis. The method of notification by newspaper announcement is merely a method that presumes the notified party can receive the notice. This method should be adopted only if at least two conditions are met: first, direct notification is impossible due to unknown address or whereabouts of the notified party; second, the law permits notification by announcement and specifies how long the announcement period must be for the notice to be deemed received. Without these two conditions, only direct written notification should be used. In this case, the original creditor, the Jinan Office of China Great Wall Asset Management Corporation, knew the addresses of the debtor and the guarantors but did not use direct written notification; instead, it used newspaper announcement without legal basis. This notification is not legally effective. According to scholarly interpretation, the method of notification of assignment of creditor's rights should be the same as the method of creation of the creditor's rights. If the creditor's rights were created in writing, the assignment of creditor's rights should also be notified to the debtor in writing. (3) The first-instance proceedings were procedurally unlawful. 1. The first instance violated the provisions of the law regarding subject matter jurisdiction and erroneously heard this case. The Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Acceptance of First-Instance Civil and Economic Dispute Cases by Higher People's Courts stipulates that the Shandong High People's Court may accept first-instance economic dispute cases only if the amount in dispute is not less than RMB 50 million. This case is an economic dispute case. The amount claimed by He Ronglan was only over RMB 30 million, which is far from the minimum amount for first-instance economic dispute cases accepted by the Shandong High People's Court. Therefore, the Shandong High People's Court should not have accepted this case. Regarding the erroneous subject matter jurisdiction in the first instance, Haike Company raised an objection to jurisdiction to the court of first instance, requesting that the case be transferred to the Dongying Intermediate People's Court of Shandong Province, which has jurisdiction. The court of first instance ignored this objection, violating the law. The first-instance judgment held that this case is a civil case and that the minimum amount for first-instance civil cases accepted by the Shandong High People's Court is RMB 30 million. This finding is erroneous. A loan contract dispute is not a civil dispute case within the meaning of the Supreme People's Court's provisions on subject matter jurisdiction; it is an economic dispute case. This case should be reversed on grounds of procedural unlawfulness and transferred to a court with jurisdiction for trial. 2. The first instance consolidated for trial several loan contract disputes with different parties, which violates the provisions of the Civil Procedure Law on joint actions. The different contract disputes should be dealt with separately. He Ronglan acquired the creditor's rights from the Jinan Office of China Great Wall Asset Management Corporation, which had acquired the creditor's rights separately from the Dongying District Sub-branch and the Hekou District Sub-branch of Agricultural Bank of China. Among these, the creditor's rights acquired from the Dongying District Sub-branch were under a loan contract guaranteed by Haike Company with a principal of RMB 10.5 million; while the creditor's rights acquired from the Hekou District Sub-branch involved three contracts, with the guarantor being the Building Materials Company. After acquiring these creditor's rights, the Jinan Office of China Great Wall Asset Management Corporation replaced the lender positions of the Dongying District Sub-branch and the Hekou District Sub-branch in each respective loan contract, becoming the creditor for different contracts. Assuming He Ronglan validly acquired the creditor's rights from the Jinan Office of China Great Wall Asset Management Corporation, she then replaced the Jinan Office's creditor position and became the creditor for different loan contracts. One contract with a principal of RMB 10.5 million was guaranteed by Haike Company; the other three contracts, with a total principal of RMB 2 million, were guaranteed by the Building Materials Company. As stated above, the borrowers under these three loan contracts had already changed their names at the time the contracts were signed in 1994, and the enterprise did not exist. Therefore, the loan contracts should be deemed invalid. For these four loan contract disputes with different parties and different contract validity, the court of first instance consolidated them for trial, which does not comply with the provisions of the Civil Procedure Law of China on joint actions and is not conducive to the correct trial of the case. In summary, Haike Company requests that He Ronglan's lawsuit be dismissed, or that the first-instance judgment be reversed and the case be transferred to the Dongying Intermediate People's Court of Shandong Province, which has jurisdiction.

He Ronglan responded, stating: (1) Haike Company's claim that the first-instance judgment had unclear findings of fact on the grounds that the Building Materials Company lacked the capacity to be a party to the lawsuit is unfounded. After He Ronglan jointly sued the Cement Products Factory, Haike Company, and the Building Materials Company, Tian Zhenrong, as the legal representative of both the Cement Products Factory and the Building Materials Company, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings and acknowledged the facts alleged by He Ronglan. As to facts not disputed by the opposing parties, Haike Company, as the guarantor of another debt, has no right to appeal regarding that part of the facts, nor does Haike Company have evidence to support its claim. In particular, the loan contracts and guarantee contracts signed between the Hekou District Sub-branch of Agricultural Bank of China and the Cement Products Factory and the Building Materials Company are unrelated to Haike Company. The validity of those loan and guarantee contracts has no legal bearing on Haike Company, and Haike Company has no right to appeal regarding them. (2) Haike Company's argument that the first-instance judgment erroneously applied the law cannot stand. As to whether notifying the debtor of the assignment of creditor's rights by newspaper announcement complies with the law, Article 6 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Cases Involving the Acquisition, Management, and Disposition of Non-performing Assets of State-owned Banks by Financial Asset Management Companies provides that if, after the financial asset management company acquires the creditor's rights of a state-owned bank, the original creditor bank publishes an announcement of the assignment of creditor's rights in a national or provincial influential newspaper, the people's court may find that the creditor has fulfilled the notification obligation under Article 80, paragraph 1 of the Contract Law. This judicial interpretation fully affirms the legality of notifying debtors of the assignment of creditor's rights by newspaper announcement. Based on the fact that the Jinan Office of China Great Wall Asset Management Corporation published a newspaper announcement of the assignment of creditor's rights and a correct understanding of Article 80, paragraph 1 of the Contract Law, the court of first instance correctly found that the original creditor, the Jinan Office of China Great Wall Asset Management Corporation, had properly and lawfully fulfilled the notification obligation of assignment of creditor's rights to the debtor, the Cement Products Factory, and the guarantors, Haike Company and the Building Materials Company, by means of a newspaper announcement. (3) Haike Company's claim that the first-instance proceedings were procedurally unlawful cannot stand. 1. Haike Company's claim that the court of first instance violated the provisions of the Civil Procedure Law on subject matter jurisdiction cannot stand. The filing division of the court of first instance, based on the legal relationship asserted by the respondent, determined that the case should be filed as a civil case, which has legal basis. The dispute over repayment of debts between He Ronglan and the Cement Products Factory, Haike Company, and the Building Materials Company in this case is a contract dispute between a natural person and legal persons, and the subject matter of the claim meets the standard (RMB 30 million or more) for the higher people's court to accept first-instance civil cases as stipulated by the Supreme People's Court. Therefore, the acceptance of this case by the court of first instance does not violate the Supreme People's Court's provisions on subject matter jurisdiction. Moreover, pursuant to Article 39 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, a higher people's court has the authority to hear first-instance civil cases under the jurisdiction of a lower people's court. Therefore, there is nothing improper about the court of first instance accepting this case. Haike Company's appellate claim that the court of first instance did not respond at all to its objection to jurisdiction does not match the facts. According to the relevant provisions of the Supreme People's Court, for objections to jurisdiction raised by parties on the issue of subject matter jurisdiction, the court receiving the case may, after reviewing whether the objection is established, directly inform the parties, without needing to issue a written ruling. The basic fact in this case is that the judge in charge of the filing division of the court of first instance, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Supreme People's Court, clearly informed Haike Company that the acceptance and filing of the case by the court of first instance did not violate the provisions on subject matter jurisdiction, that Haike Company's objection to subject matter jurisdiction was not established, and thus orally rejected Haike Company's objection to jurisdiction. With respect to the subsequent written "Application for Objection to Jurisdiction," the filing division of the court of first instance, having already given a clear response on the issue, directly transferred the case file to the First Civil Division for trial. After the case file was transferred to the First Civil Division, the judge in charge also clearly informed Haike Company that the objection to jurisdiction was not established and that Haike Company should appear in court in a timely manner to participate in the proceedings. The fact that Haike Company appeared in court twice to fully cross-examine the evidence submitted by He Ronglan and the appraisal report commissioned by the court of first instance also proves that the court of first instance did not fail to respond to the issue. Haike Company accepted the subject matter jurisdiction of the court of first instance through its active litigation conduct. The court of first instance carefully tried the case, gave full consideration to Haike Company's cross-examination opinions, and rendered a fair judgment. 2. Haike Company's claim that this case cannot be consolidated for trial cannot stand. Consolidation for trial refers to the joinder of claims, which can be divided into two types: joinder of parties and joinder of objects. Haike Company, as a guarantor, is a party in a necessary joint action, and Haike Company's participation in this case constitutes a joinder of parties. Since the borrower, i.e., the debtor, under the loan contracts involved in this case is the Cement Products Factory, consolidating for trial in this case the several loan debts covered by the assigned creditor's rights as a whole constitutes a joinder of objects. In this case, the creditor is He Ronglan, and the debtor is the Cement Products Factory alone. The creditor-debtor relationship between the parties is clear. Although the guarantors in this case, Haike Company and the Building Materials Company, are not the same entity, the debts for which each guarantor is separately liable are clear, and the joint and several liability that each should bear within the scope of the debts they respectively guarantee is also clear. Consolidation for trial does not harm any of Haike Company's litigation rights. Therefore, the consolidation for trial by the court of first instance complies with the relevant provisions of the law. In summary, the first-instance judgment had clear findings of fact and correctly applied the law. Haike Company's appellate claims lack evidence and are improperly grounded. He Ronglan requests that the court of second instance reject the appeal according to law and affirm the original judgment.

The Cement Products Factory and the Building Materials Company did not submit a written defense.

The facts found by this Court are the same as those found by the court of first instance.

This Court is of the opinion that: The debt assignment contract signed between He Ronglan and the Jinan Office of China Great Wall Asset Management Corporation on September 30, 2002, was a true expression of the parties' intention, and its content does not violate the mandatory provisions of laws and regulations. The judgment of the court of first instance correctly upheld the validity of the debt assignment contract. Haike Company, in its appeal, raised an objection regarding the issue of level jurisdiction in this case. Since level jurisdiction concerns the division of work between higher and lower courts in the handling of first-instance cases, when a party raises an objection to level jurisdiction, the court receiving the action shall carefully examine the matter; if it indeed lacks jurisdiction, it shall transfer the case to the court with jurisdiction and notify the parties, but shall not make a ruling. The above provisions indicate that although a party has the right to raise an objection to level jurisdiction, it does not have a right of action in respect of such objection. A party may not initiate a claim by way of an objection to level jurisdiction, nor does it have the right to appeal after the objection is dismissed. The level jurisdiction objection raised by Haike Company to the court of first instance was replied to by that court and recorded in the case file. The appellate request of Haike Company concerning the issue of level jurisdiction exceeds the scope of the appeal requests a party may raise, and therefore should not be upheld. Haike Company further contends in its appeal that the Cement Products Factory and the Building Materials Company are in fact the same entity, and therefore the Building Materials Company lacks the qualification to be a party to the lawsuit, and that the guarantee loan contract signed between the Hekou Sub-branch of the Agricultural Bank of China Dongying City, the Cement Products Factory, and the Building Materials Company should be held invalid. During the proceedings of the first instance, neither the Cement Products Factory, the Building Materials Company, nor He Ronglan raised any objection to the qualification of the Building Materials Company as a litigation party. After the judgment of the first instance, He Ronglan, the Cement Products Factory, and the Building Materials Company did not appeal the issue of the Building Materials Company's qualification. Haike Company is not a party to the said guarantee loan contract, and it has no evidence that the guarantee loan contract harms the rights and interests of Haike Company. Whether the Building Materials Company has the qualification to be a party to the lawsuit and the validity of the guarantee loan contract have no legal interest relationship with Haike Company. Therefore, this Court will not uphold this claim of Haike Company. Haike Company claims that the two debt disputes involved in this case should not have been consolidated for trial. Since the consolidation of actions may be based either on a party's application or on a decision by the people's court, in this case, the two debt disputes have the same creditor (He Ronglan), the same debtor (the Cement Products Factory), and the same nature of the creditor-debtor relationship. Both disputes fall within the jurisdiction of the court of first instance. It was not improper for the court of first instance to consolidate the two debt disputes for trial. Haike Company's argument that the consolidation was erroneous solely because the guarantors for the debts were different lacks sufficient basis and should be dismissed. In this case, He Ronglan, as the creditor, brought the action against the debtor and the guarantor based on the debt assignment contract she concluded with the Jinan Office of China Great Wall Asset Management Corporation, thereby acquiring the status of creditor and initiating the civil lawsuit in that capacity. After the judgment of the first instance, neither He Ronglan (the creditor), the Cement Products Factory (the debtor), nor the Building Materials Company (the guarantor) filed an appeal. Neither He Ronglan, the Cement Products Factory, the Building Materials Company, nor Haike Company raised any objection to the validity of the debt assignment after the judgment of the first instance. Haike Company claims that the assignment of the debt was not notified to the debtor and the guarantor, and therefore the validity of the debt assignment does not extend to Haike Company. Paragraph 1 of Article 80 of the Contract Law provides that if a creditor assigns its rights, it shall notify the debtor. Without notification, the assignment is not binding on the debtor. However, laws and regulations do not specify the exact method of notification. The actual circumstances of this case are that after the Jinan Office of China Great Wall Asset Management Corporation assigned its creditor's rights to He Ronglan, the two parties jointly published a notice of the debt assignment in the Shandong Legal News to inform the debtor and the guarantor. The Shandong Legal News is a publicly and widely distributed newspaper within Shandong Province. The court of first instance held that it was not contrary to the mandatory provisions of laws or regulations for the creditor to publish a notice in such a newspaper to inform the debtor and the guarantor of the debt assignment, and there is nothing improper in that finding. Moreover, in this case, the assignor of the creditor's rights, the assignee, the debtor, and the guarantor have all raised no objection to the fact or validity of the debt assignment. The debtor and the guarantor only disputed the amount of interest on the debt, which was examined and dealt with by the court of first instance. In its appellate request, Haike Company did not raise any objection concerning the content or validity of the debt assignment; that is, Haike Company recognized the existence of the debt between the parties. Through its participation in the proceedings of this case, Haike Company was fully aware of the fact of the debt assignment and knew the party to whom the debt should be performed. The debt assignment in this case did not cause the debtor to perform the debt erroneously, to perform the debt twice, or to increase the burden of performance on the debtor, nor did it harm the interests of Haike Company. The rights and obligations between the parties are clear, and the debtor and the guarantor shall bear corresponding legal liability. Haike Company's denial of the binding effect of the debt assignment on it solely on the ground that the creditor's notice of assignment was published in a newspaper is insufficiently reasoned and will not be upheld by this Court. In summary, the facts found by the court of first instance are clear and the application of law is correct. In accordance with Item (1) of Paragraph 1 of Article 153 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

Appeal dismissed; the original judgment is affirmed.

Court acceptance fee for the second instance: RMB 168,928, to be borne by Haike Company.

This judgment is final.
